title: NTD-identification
text: Normalized event studies widely used labor economics compare treatment effects across groups different baseline levels (e.g., comparing earnings penalties childbirth men women). standard approach divides effects earnings levels make comparable. vignette demonstrates: identification assumption makes normalized comparisons valid bias structure emerges normalizing bias behaves comparing across groups ’ll use simple data generating process (DGP) visualize exactly bias comes matters.

what: Setup: A DGP where normalized parallel trends holds
title: NTD-identification
text: create world : Two genders: women men (men earning ) Two treatment cohorts: early (D=25) late (D=30) Linear earnings growth (late cohorts steeper slopes) Treatment effects (earnings penalties childbirth) key design feature: ratios preserved normalized parallel trends violations equal across gender.
code: # Parameters baseline    <- 500 ratio_bias  <- 3    # late vs early slope multiplier ratio_apos  <- 3    # men vs women slope multiplier ages        <- 20:30 d_early     <- 25 d_late      <- 30  # Counterfactual earning slopes s_f_25 <- baseline s_f_30 <- baseline * ratio_bias s_m_25 <- baseline * ratio_apos s_m_30 <- baseline * ratio_apos * ratio_bias  # Treatment effects (ATT) att_f  <- -6000 att_m  <- -2000  # Build each group make_group <- function(sex, D, slope, att_level) {   tibble(     age    = ages,     female = sex,     D      = D,     y_0    = slope * age,           # counterfactual (no treatment)     y_1    = y_0 + ifelse(age >= D, att_level, 0),     y      = y_1                     # observed   ) }  data <- bind_rows(   make_group(1, d_early, s_f_25, att_f),   make_group(1, d_late,  s_f_30, att_f),   make_group(0, d_early, s_m_25, att_m),   make_group(0, d_late,  s_m_30, att_m) )

title: NTD-identification
text: visualizing bias, let’s verify DGP actually satisfies normalized parallel trends assumption.

title: NTD-identification
text: First, let’s calculate parallel trend violation levels - difference counterfactual trends early late treated within gender:  Key observation: parallel trends violations levels equal across gender. Men’s violations much larger higher baseline earnings. violates standard parallel trends.
code: # Calculate trend from pre-treatment (age D-1) to each subsequent age trends <- function(g, d, a) {   pre <- data |> filter(D == d, female == g, age == d-1) |> pull(y_0)   post <- data |> filter(D == d, female == g, age == a) |> pull(y_0)   post - pre }  # Difference in trends between early and late cohorts diff_trends <- function(g, a) trends(g, 25, a) - trends(g, 30, a)  expand_grid(   female = c(0, 1),   age    = ages ) |>   mutate(     diff_trend = purrr::map2_dbl(female, age, diff_trends),     gender = factor(if_else(female == 1, "Women", "Men"), levels = c("Women", "Men"))   ) |>    ggplot(aes(x = age, y = diff_trend, color = gender)) +    geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +    labs(     title = "Parallel Trends Violation in Levels",     subtitle = "Different across gender → standard parallel trends fails",     x = "Age",      y = "Difference in counterfactual trends (dollars)",      color = "Gender"   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: NTD-identification
text: Now let’s normalize dividing average potential earnings (APO) absence treatment:  Critical result: normalized parallel trends violations identical men women every age. lines overlap perfectly. exactly NTD (normalized triple differences) identification assumption requires. work? construction, late cohort slopes constant multiple early slopes (within gender), men’s slopes constant multiple women’s slopes (within cohort). constant multiples cancel take ratios, ensuring normalized PT violations equal across gender.
code: # Get counterfactual earnings for early cohort (APO) get_apo <- function(g, a) {   data |>     dplyr::filter(D == 25, female == g, age == a) |>     dplyr::pull(y_0) }  expand_grid(   female = c(0, 1),   age    = ages ) |>   mutate(     diff_trend = purrr::map2_dbl(female, age, diff_trends),     y_0 = purrr::map2_dbl(female, age, get_apo),     norm_diff_trend = diff_trend / y_0,     gender = factor(if_else(female == 1, "Women", "Men"), levels = c("Women", "Men"))   ) |>    ggplot(aes(x = age, y = norm_diff_trend, color = gender)) +    geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +    labs(     title = "Normalized Parallel Trends Violation",     subtitle = "Identical across gender → NTD assumption holds!",     x = "Age",      y = "Normalized difference (proportion of earnings)",      color = "Gender"   ) +   scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

what: The Setup - Counterfactuals and Observed Data
title: NTD-identification
text: Let’s start seeing observe vs. true counterfactuals:  Key observations: solid blue line shows observe early cohort treatment age 25 Light blue dashed: happened without treatment (early cohort) Orange dashed: happened late cohort (different slope!) gap solid light blue dashed = true treatment effect problem: don’t observe light blue line. need impute somehow.
code: plot_df <- bind_rows(   # Early cohort: observed and counterfactual   data %>%     filter(D == d_early) %>%     pivot_longer(cols = c(y_0, y), names_to = "series", values_to = "value"),   # Late cohort: counterfactual only (not yet treated at these ages for early cohort)   data %>%     filter(D == d_late) %>%     transmute(age, female, D, series = "y_0", value = y_0) ) %>%   mutate(     gender = factor(if_else(female == 1, "Women", "Men"), levels = c("Women", "Men")),     cohort = factor(if_else(D == d_early, "Early (D=25)", "Late (D=30)"),                     levels = c("Early (D=25)", "Late (D=30)")),     series_label = case_when(       cohort == "Early (D=25)" & series == "y"   ~ "Early — Observed",       cohort == "Early (D=25)" & series == "y_0" ~ "Early — Counterfactual",       cohort == "Late (D=30)"  & series == "y_0" ~ "Late — Counterfactual"     ),     linetype = if_else(series_label == "Early — Observed", "solid", "dashed"),     color = case_when(       series_label == "Early — Observed"       ~ "Obs.",       series_label == "Early — Counterfactual" ~ "CF Early",       TRUE                                     ~ "CF Late"     )   )  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = age, y = value, group = series_label)) +   geom_line(aes(linetype = linetype, color = color), linewidth = 1.1) +   facet_wrap(~ gender, nrow = 1) +   scale_linetype_identity() +   scale_color_manual(     values = c("Obs." = "#1f77b4", "CF Early" = "#9ecae1", "CF Late" = "#fdae6b")   ) +   labs(     title = "Figure 1: Observed vs. Counterfactual Earnings",     x = "Age", y = "Earnings", color = NULL   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

what: The DID Approach - Using Late Cohort as Control
title: NTD-identification
text: Standard difference--differences uses late cohort impute counterfactual early cohort:  key insight: green line (imputation) doesn’t match light blue line (truth). difference parallel trends bias - happens late cohort steeper slope. Important property DGP: divide green line light blue dashed line, get ratio men women every age. implication thee normalized parallel trends assumption.
code: # Calculate DID-imputed counterfactual did_cf <- bind_rows(lapply(c(1, 0), function(g) {   # Early cohort's pre-treatment level   early_pre <- data %>%     filter(female == g, D == d_early, age == d_early - 1) %>%     pull(y)      # Late cohort trend   late_cf <- data %>% filter(female == g, D == d_late) %>% select(age, y_0)   late_pre <- late_cf %>% filter(age == d_early - 1) %>% pull(y_0)      # DID imputation: shift late trend to match early pre-treatment level   tibble(     age    = late_cf$age,     female = g,     D      = d_early,     series = "y_cf_did",     value  = early_pre + (late_cf$y_0 - late_pre)   ) })) %>%   mutate(     gender = factor(if_else(female == 1, "Women", "Men"), levels = c("Women", "Men")),     cohort = factor("Early (D=25)", levels = c("Early (D=25)", "Late (D=30)")),     series_label = "Early — DID-imputed CF",     linetype = "dotdash",     color = "CF DID"   )  plot_df_plus <- bind_rows(plot_df, did_cf)  ggplot(plot_df_plus, aes(x = age, y = value, group = series_label)) +   geom_line(aes(linetype = linetype, color = color), linewidth = 1.1) +   facet_wrap(~ gender, nrow = 1) +   scale_linetype_identity() +   scale_color_manual(     values = c(       "Obs." = "#1f77b4", "CF Early" = "#9ecae1",        "CF Late" = "#fdae6b", "CF DID" = "#2ca02c"     )   ) +   labs(     title = "Figure 2: DID-Imputed Counterfactual",     subtitle = "Green line = what DID thinks would have happened without treatment",     x = "Age", y = "Earnings", color = NULL   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

what: Decomposing DID Estimates into Truth and Bias
title: NTD-identification
text: Let’s break gives us. age, can decompose: APO (average potential outcome) = Truth - PT Bias ATE (average treatment effect) = Truth + PT Bias  shows: APO row: estimates counterfactual earnings = True counterfactual (blue) minus PT bias (orange) ATE row: estimates treatment effects = True effect (blue) plus PT bias (orange) bias opposite signs counterfactual overshoots truth (steeper slope).
code: # Calculate true APO and ATE early_true_age <- data %>%   filter(D == d_early) %>%   group_by(female, age) %>%   summarise(APO_true = y_0, ATE_true = y - y_0, .groups = "drop")  # Calculate DID APO early_did_age <- did_cf %>%   group_by(female, age) %>%   summarise(APO_did = value, .groups = "drop")  # Combine and calculate bias summary_age <- early_true_age %>%   left_join(early_did_age, by = c("female", "age")) %>%   mutate(     PT_bias = APO_true - APO_did,  # parallel trends bias     ATE_did = ATE_true + PT_bias,  # DID ATE = truth + bias     gender  = factor(if_else(female == 1, "Women", "Men"), levels = c("Women", "Men"))   )  # Prepare stacked bar chart data apo_stack_age <- summary_age %>%   transmute(     gender, age = factor(age),     measure = factor("APO", levels = c("APO", "ATE")),     total = APO_did, comp_true = APO_true, comp_bias = -PT_bias   ) %>%   pivot_longer(c(comp_true, comp_bias), names_to = "component", values_to = "value") %>%   mutate(component = if_else(component == "comp_true", "Truth", "PT bias"))  ate_stack_age <- summary_age %>%   transmute(     gender, age = factor(age),     measure = factor("ATE", levels = c("APO", "ATE")),     total = ATE_did, comp_true = ATE_true, comp_bias = PT_bias   ) %>%   pivot_longer(c(comp_true, comp_bias), names_to = "component", values_to = "value") %>%   mutate(component = if_else(component == "comp_true", "Truth", "PT bias"))  bar_age_df <- bind_rows(apo_stack_age, ate_stack_age)  ggplot(bar_age_df, aes(x = age, y = value, fill = component)) +   geom_col(width = 0.7) +   facet_grid(rows = vars(measure), cols = vars(gender), scales = "free_y") +   scale_fill_manual(     values = c("Truth" = "#1f77b4", "PT bias" = "#fdae6b"),     breaks = c("Truth", "PT bias")   ) +   labs(     title = "Decomposing DID",     subtitle = "Top row: DID APO (DID imputed counterfactual earnings) | Bottom row: DID ATE (DID imputed treatment effect)",     x = "Age", y = NULL, fill = NULL   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

text: Now key question: happens normalize? normalized event studies, compute: δθ=ATEDID APO\delta_{\theta} = \frac{\text{ATE}}{\text{APO}} meant estimate true ratio: θ=True ATETrue APO\theta = \frac{\text{True ATE}}{\text{True APO}} Let’s see bias emerges compute δθ\delta_{\theta}.

title: NTD-identification
text: Note δθ=ATEDID APO=TRUE ATE+PT BiasDID APO=TRUE ATEDID APO+PT BiasDID APO\delta_{\theta} = \frac{\text{ATE}}{\text{APO}}=\frac{\text{TRUE ATE} + \text{PT Bias}}{\text{APO}}=\frac{\text{TRUE ATE}}{\text{APO}}+\frac{\text{PT Bias}}{\text{APO}} now analyze TRUE ATEDID APO+PT BiasDID APO\frac{\text{TRUE ATE}}{\text{APO}}+\frac{\text{PT Bias}}{\text{APO}}. Since sum, go one one. Start PT BiasDID APO\frac{\text{PT Bias}}{\text{APO}}.  Critical observation: bottom row (PT / APO) identical men women every age. Hence, differencing across gender cancels bias parameter. implication NTD assumption.
code: pt_ratio_df <- summary_age %>%   transmute(     gender, age = factor(age),     measure = factor("Ratios", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios")),     component = "PT / DID APO",     value = PT_bias / pmax(APO_true - PT_bias, .Machine$double.eps)   )  bar_age_three <- bind_rows(   apo_stack_age %>% mutate(measure = factor("APO", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios"))),   ate_stack_age %>% mutate(measure = factor("ATE", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios"))),   pt_ratio_df )  ggplot(bar_age_three, aes(x = age, y = value, fill = component)) +   geom_col(width = 0.7) +   facet_grid(rows = vars(measure), cols = vars(gender), scales = "free_y") +   scale_fill_manual(     values = c(       "Truth" = "#1f77b4", "PT bias" = "#fdae6b", "PT / DID APO" = "#99d8c9"     )   ) +   labs(     title = "Figure 4: Normalizing the PT Bias",     subtitle = "Bottom row shows PT bias / DID APO",     x = "Age", y = NULL, fill = NULL   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: NTD-identification
text: Now let’s add second part sum, ATEDID APO\frac{\text{ATE}}{\text{APO}}.  bottom row shows: Light teal (PT / APO): across gender →\rightarrow cancels difference gender Dark green (ATE / APO): Different across gender →\rightarrow now need understand, difference gender, much bias? much effect?
code: ratios_df <- summary_age %>%   transmute(     gender, age = factor(age),     measure = factor("Ratios", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios")),     `PT ratio`  = PT_bias / pmax(APO_true - PT_bias, .Machine$double.eps),     `ATE ratio` = ATE_true / pmax(APO_true - PT_bias, .Machine$double.eps)   ) %>%   pivot_longer(     cols = c(`PT ratio`, `ATE ratio`),      names_to = "component",      values_to = "value"   )  bar_age_three2 <- bind_rows(   apo_stack_age %>% mutate(measure = factor("APO", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios"))),   ate_stack_age %>% mutate(measure = factor("ATE", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios"))),   ratios_df )  ggplot(bar_age_three2, aes(x = age, y = value, fill = component)) +   geom_col(width = 0.7) +   facet_grid(rows = vars(measure), cols = vars(gender), scales = "free_y") +   scale_fill_manual(     values = c(       "Truth" = "#1f77b4", "PT bias" = "#fdae6b",       "PT ratio" = "#99d8c9", "ATE ratio" = "#2ca25f"     )   ) +   labs(     title = "Figure 5: Complete Decomposition of the Normalized Ratio",     subtitle = "Bottom row: Light teal (drops out when differencing) + Dark green (what remains)",     x = "Age", y = NULL, fill = NULL   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: NTD-identification
text: ’s gets interesting. dark green component (ATE / APO) can rewritten reveal multiplicative bias: ATEDID APO=ATETrue APO−PT bias=θ⋅True APOTrue APO−PT bias\frac{\text{ATE}}{\text{APO}} = \frac{\text{ATE}}{\text{True APO} - \text{PT bias}} = \theta \cdot \frac{\text{True APO}}{\text{True APO} - \text{PT bias}} θ=True ATE/True APO\theta = \text{True ATE} / \text{True APO} true ratio want. simplifies : ATEDID APO=θ+θ⋅PT biasTrue APO−PT bias\frac{\text{ATE}}{\text{APO}} = \theta + \theta \cdot \frac{\text{PT bias}}{\text{True APO} - \text{PT bias}} second term multiplicative bias - true effect gets scaled ratio PT bias APO. discussed , quantity PT biasTrue APO−PT bias\frac{\text{PT bias}}{\text{True APO} - \text{PT bias}} constant genders. genders treatment effects scaled factor.  Bottom row interpretation: Blue (Truth): true ratio θ\theta want estimate Teal (Bias ): PT / APO - drops differencing across gender Green (Bias B): θ×PT biasTrue APO−PT bias\theta \times \frac{\text{PT bias}}{\text{True APO} - \text{PT bias}} - equal gender, since θ\theta allowed different gender →\rightarrow hence bias remains differencing
code: eps <- .Machine$double.eps  theta_df <- summary_age %>%   transmute(     gender, age = factor(age),     APO_true, ATE_true, APO_did, PT_bias,     theta_true = ATE_true / pmax(APO_true, eps),     bias_A = PT_bias / pmax(APO_true - PT_bias, eps),     bias_B = theta_true * (APO_true / pmax(APO_true - PT_bias, eps) - 1)   )  theta_stack <- bind_rows(   theta_df %>% transmute(     gender, age, measure = factor("Ratios", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios")),     component = "Truth", value = theta_true   ),   theta_df %>% transmute(     gender, age, measure = factor("Ratios", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios")),     component = "Bias A", value = bias_A   ),   theta_df %>% transmute(     gender, age, measure = factor("Ratios", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios")),     component = "Bias B", value = bias_B   ) )  bar_age_three3 <- bind_rows(   apo_stack_age %>% mutate(measure = factor("APO", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios"))),   ate_stack_age %>% mutate(measure = factor("ATE", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios"))),   theta_stack )  ggplot(bar_age_three3, aes(x = age, y = value, fill = component)) +   geom_col(width = 0.7) +   facet_grid(rows = vars(measure), cols = vars(gender), scales = "free_y") +   scale_fill_manual(     values = c(       "Truth" = "#1f77b4", "PT bias" = "#fdae6b",       "Bias A" = "#99d8c9", "Bias B" = "#2ca25f"     ),     breaks = c("Truth", "PT bias", "Bias A", "Bias B"),     labels = c("Truth", "PT bias", "PT / DID APO", "Truth × Bias")   ) +   labs(     title = "Figure 6: The Multiplicative Bias Structure",     subtitle = "Bottom row: Blue (true θ) + Teal (drops out) + Green (multiplicative bias)",     x = "Age", y = NULL, fill = NULL   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: NTD-identification
text: normalization creates multiplicative bias: Even identifying assumption holds, estimated ratio contains bias scales true effect bias structure: Additive part (teal): Cancels differencing across groups Multiplicative part (green): Remains differencing Magnitude matters: multiplicative bias θ⋅λ1−λ\theta \cdot \frac{\lambda}{1-\lambda} λ=PT bias/True APO\lambda = \text{PT bias} / \text{True APO}. λ\lambda increases, bias increases. size PT violations crucial interpreting normalized event study estimates.

title: Simulating Child Penalty Data
text: DGP supposed serve realistic DGP simulations studies child penalty applications. goal construct life-cycle earning profiles potential earnings observed treatment counterfactual treatment never child. problem identifying life-cycle patterns counterfactual earnings diffcult. DGP simplifying assumptions, construct process creates life-cycle earnings, motivated empirical data. Using Israeli administrative data, mean earnings triplets (gender, treatment group, age) estimated. Mens mean earnings fit cubic polynomials. Assume men zero treatment effect. Assign mean counterfactual earnings men using means observed outcomes. Assume womens’ mean counterfactual earnings, within treatment group, equal men age 27. title: Unconditional estimands for a single treatment group — single_treatment_group_analysis
text: data.frame one row per estimand/method combination: estimand — one "APO", "ATE", "theta" method — one "DID_Female", "DID_Male", "TD", "NTD", "NTD_Alt", "TD_Null", "NTD_Null" est — estimate se — cluster-robust standard error n_female_treat, n_female_control, n_male_treat, n_male_control — sample counts

title: Unconditional estimands for a single treatment group — single_treatment_group_analysis
text: Let \(Y(, g, d^\star)\) denote mean outcome age \(\) gender \(g \\{0,1\}\) (1 = female) assigned group \(d^\star\). core components : APO(g; d, d', ) \(= Y(d-\mathrm{pre}, g, d) + Y(, g, d') - Y(d-\mathrm{pre}, g, d')\) ATE(g; d, d', ) \(= Y(, g, d) - \mathrm{APO}(g; d, d', )\) \(\theta\)(g) \(= \mathrm{ATE}(g) / \mathrm{APO}(g)\) , cross-gender contrasts formed: TD \(= \mathrm{ATE}(F) - \mathrm{ATE}(M)\) NTD \(= \theta(F) - \theta(M)\) NTD Alt \(= \frac{Y(,F,d)}{Y(,M,d)} - \frac{\mathrm{APO}(F)}{\mathrm{APO}(M)}\) TD Null NTD Null variants defined analogously null-effect--fathers bias-correction. Internally, influence functions pieces written temporary columns data.table via compute_mean_if(), cluster-robust standard errors computed summing IFs id level via se_cluster().

title: Unconditional estimands for a single treatment group — single_treatment_group_analysis
text: Requires helper functions compute_mean_if() se_cluster().

title: Unconditional estimands for a single treatment group — single_treatment_group_analysis
